description:
Most people spend all their energy on what to say - but the room starts reading you the moment you walk in. 

In this Quick Thinks episode of Think Fast, Talk Smart, host Matt Abrahams walks you through the fundamentals of confidence in communication and how to hold your body while speaking.

In this episode, Matt covers:
• There's a specific physical "starting stance" for speaking that most people have never been taught.
• What you do with your feet may be silently broadcasting your nerves.
• The place you rest your hands when you aren't gesturing matters A LOT.
• A simple one-rule test for whether your gesture is helping or hurting your credibility
• Instead of looking up when you need to think, do the opposite!
• Watching yourself on video is the highest-leverage practice - if done correctly.
The research-backed framework Matt shares in the episode is concise, specific, and immediately actionable - the kind of checklist you can run through in your head right before your next presentation, meeting, or high-stakes conversation! 

About Matt
Matt Abrahams is a leading communication expert, Lecturer in Organisational Behaviour at Stanford GSB, and host of the award-winning Think Fast, Talk Smart podcast. He has coached presenters at TED, the World Economic Forum, and the UN Secretary General's office, and his online talks have garnered millions of views worldwide. He is the author of Think Faster, Talk Smarter and Speaking Up without Freaking Out — two bestselling guides to confident, spontaneous communication.

Key Quotes
• "Your presence at times can speak louder than your words." - Matt Abrahams (00:00)
• “It took me a long time, years, to be comfortable talking with my hands down by my side." - Matt Abrahams (03:56)
• "Think of your chest as a basketball key. If you know the rules of basketball, you can be in the key for 3 seconds without getting a penalty." - Matt Abrahams (5:15)
• "It is better to look down than look up. When I look down, I look thoughtful and pensive. When I look up, I look confused." - Matt Abrahams (07:04)
